provenance.title: Draft of June 11, 2024 A QUANTUM MURNAGHAN–NAKAYAMA RULE FOR THE FLAG MANIFOLD
provenance.authors: C. BENEDETTI, N. BERGERON, L. COLMENAREJO, F. SALIOLA, AND F. SOTTILE

candidates.statement: ::: proof *Proof.* For $u,w \in S_n$, a partition $\lambda$, $k \in {\mathbb N}$ with $1\leq k$ and $\alpha\in {\mathbb N}^{n-1}$, define quantum Littlewood--Richardson coefficients $C^{q^\alpha w}_{u,v(\lambda,k)}\in q^\alpha {\mathbb N}$ by $$\label{eq-definition-Cq} {\mathfrak S}_u \ast s^q_\lambda(x_1, \ldots, x_k) \ =\ \sum_{q^\alpha w \in S_n[q]} C^{q^\alpha w}_{u,v(\lambda,k)} {\mathfrak S}_w\,.$$ We must prove that

As $N^{w,\alpha}_{u,v(\lambda,k)}\neq 0$, Proposition [\[P:LL_Th1.1\]](#P:LL_Th1.1){reference-type="ref" reference="P:LL_Th1.1"}(1) implies that $${\mbox{\rm sg}}_i(w)\ =\ 0\,,\ \ \ \varpi_i(\alpha)\ =\ 2\,,\ \ \mbox{and}\ \ {\mbox{\rm sg}}_i(u)\ =\ {\mbox{\rm sg}}_i(v(\lambda,k))\ = \ 1\,.$$ Since ${\mbox{\rm sg}}_i(v(\lambda,k))=1$, we must have that $i=k$, as $v(\lambda,k)$ has a unique descent at $k$.

Since ${\mathbf v}_{cb}\mathop{\mathrm{{\scriptstyle \bullet}}}_{k}v\neq{\mathbf 0}$, not only must $c$ be left of $\raisebox{-1pt}{\hspace{0.55pt}\color{magenta}\rule{0.75pt}{11pt}}\hspace{0.55pt}$ and $b$ right of $\raisebox{-1pt}{\hspace{0.55pt}\color{magenta}\rule{0.75pt}{11pt}}\hspace{0.55pt}$, but every value $e$ of $v$ at a position between those of $c$ and $b$ satisfies $b<e<c$.

Since ${\mathbf v}_{ba}\mathop{\mathrm{{\scriptstyle \bullet}}}_{k}v\neq{\mathbf 0}$, $b$ must be left of $\raisebox{-1pt}{\hspace{0.55pt}\color{magenta}\rule{0.75pt}{11pt}}\hspace{0.55pt}$ and hence left of $c$.
Similarly, if $b_1$ is an endpoint, then we must have $a_i=b_{i+1}$ for all $i$.
By Corollary [\[T\*vq=0\]](#T*vq=0){reference-type="ref" reference="T*vq=0"}, we must have $a < a_r < \dotsb < a_1 < b$.
